About

Profile

ML Research Scientist with a Ph.D. and 4+ years developing and commercializing production ML systems on wearable and clinical time-series data. Deep expertise in deep learning, time-series analysis, signal processing, and multimodal fusion across IMU, physiological, and sensor streams: the core data modalities behind modern wearable health products.

Track record spanning the full model lifecycle, from exploratory research and pipeline design to rigorous statistical validation and production deployment in high-stakes healthcare and real-world environments. 27+ peer-reviewed publications, 650+ citations, and 5 patent filings (1 published). Currently building clinical AI models for Parkinson's disease on wearable-derived time-series data at Oregon Health & Science University.

Core technical expertise

Wearable & time-series ML
IMU / accelerometer / gyroscope pipelines, physiological waveform analysis, signal processing (filtering, denoising, feature engineering), temporal deep learning (Transformers, RNN-LSTM, 1D-CNN), windowing & segmentation, robust validation on heterogeneous subject populations
Deep learning
Transformers, CNN, RNN-LSTM, self-supervised & semi-supervised learning, transfer learning, multimodal fusion, foundation models, fine-tuning, distillation
Healthcare & clinical data
Wearable sensor time-series, clinical assessments, EMR / clinical report processing, fall-risk and neurological impairment modeling, multi-subject longitudinal studies
Statistical modeling & validation
Hypothesis testing, error estimation, performance monitoring, cross-subject generalization, A/B-style model comparison, calibration, drift detection
Programming & frameworks
Python (5+ years), SQL (5+ years), PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, OpenCV, MATLAB, C++
MLOps & deployment
End-to-end ML pipelines, large-scale dataset curation, containerized deployment, model monitoring, Azure ML / Azure OpenAI Foundry, reproducible experimentation

Work

Selected work

Research taken all the way to deployment, in industry and in the clinic.

Production ML · Hitachi America

Multimodal deep learning system, prototype to full rollout

Led end-to-end research, training, rigorous validation, and production deployment of a multimodal deep learning system that automated a complex bottleneck process in a live operational environment, working with scientists, software engineers, product managers, and test engineers.

  • 25% cycle-time reduction in a live operational environment
  • Evaluation framework with error estimation, subgroup performance analysis, and production monitoring for robustness across heterogeneous populations
  • 500+ hours/year of deployment data collected, curated, and managed; reproducible training and evaluation pipelines from heterogeneous sensor and vision streams

Wearable sensing · Computer vision

Wearable + vision multimodal perception

Multimodal perception systems that fuse IMU wearable streams (accelerometer, gyroscope) with computer vision, applying signal processing, feature engineering, and deep temporal models.

  • >90% classification accuracy across diverse real-world users
  • Proof-of-concept sensing ideas translated into deployed, commercialized features through data exploration, ablation studies, and statistical validation

Clinical AI · OHSU

Wearable-sensor AI for Parkinson's disease

Developing sensor-based deep learning models to analyze freezing of gait and fall risk in Parkinson's disease, applying time-series ML and signal processing to wearable-derived data in a research-to-deployment pipeline alongside clinicians and medical domain experts.

  • Bridging quantitative modeling with clinical knowledge for patient-centered model design, validation strategy, and interpretation of health-relevant signals

Published patent · US 2026/0198641 A1

Smart-sole wearable for ground-reaction-force sensing

In-shoe pressure-sensing architecture that computes ground reaction force, produces posture-adjustment recommendations, and unifies coordinates for foot positions and gestures. Co-invented with Q. Zhou; published Jul 16, 2026.

Ph.D. research · RIT

Machine learning for fall-risk assessment in stroke survivors

Designed and led a data-driven fall-risk assessment model using 8 IMU sensors, common clinical tests, and motor-cognitive dual-tasking; led clinical data collection at Unity Hospital with patients with neurological conditions.

  • Multiple top-journal publications and a defended Ph.D. dissertation
  • Related agendas: camera-based fall-risk assessment, smartphone fatigue detection (SVM, 91%), low-back-pain patient classification (SVM/MLP, 75%)

Transformers · Structured data

Transformer models for structured operational and report data

Designed and built Transformer-based models on structured operational and report data for classification, anomaly detection, and quality assessment; pipelines directly analogous to clinical NLP over EMRs and structured health records.

Early work · Aster Pet Sciences

Real-time IMU activity recognition, shipped

Led data collection, feature engineering, model design, and shipment of a real-time IMU-based activity recognition system (SVM, >70% accuracy) in 2021; first full ownership of an AI research-to-product pipeline.
